diagnosis: N2 BREACH in the DIMACS frontend, UNIT shape. ingest_clause applied set semantics (sort+unique) to every input clause, so the clause we STORE under input id i is not the clause the CHECKER reads from the file at position i. Here clause 1 is `-1 -1 0`: we store the unit ¬x1 under id 1, the checker holds a two-entry clause. Every LRAT chain citing id 1 then asks the checker to unit-propagate a clause that is not unit FOR IT -- checkers treat a clause as a literal LIST, not a set -- and it rejects with `multiple literals unassigned in hint 1: -2 -2` (lrat-check) / `clause not empty or singleton after reduction` (cake_lpr). DRAT is blind to it: drat-trim re-derives each lemma by RUP instead of citing ids, so the standing native-DRAT legs were green, and the native-LRAT legs only started reporting it once fuzz.py's oracle stopped accepting `c NOT VERIFIED` (same day, §6a of the Sweep report). Frequency before the fix: 1.5-4% of UNSAT fuzz cases. FIX (2026-08-05): the deduped clause is emitted as its own one-antecedent RUP lemma -- valid because negating it falsifies every literal of the file form -- and the stored id is re-pointed to the lemma. The lemma id must exceed EVERY input id and N is unknown until the input ends, so the restatements are buffered and flushed by frontend/parse.hpp's finish_input at end-of-input, which also defers the parse-time refutation (that used to burn an id the checker had already given to a later input clause). THIS CASE: pre-fix `5 0 1 4 0` is REJECTED by lrat-check AND cake_lpr; post-fix `5 -1 0 1 0` + `6 0 5 4 0` verifies under lrat-check, cake_lpr and drat-trim. Companion entry 014 covers the non-unit shape. Report: benchmarks/reports/2026-08-05-input-clause-normalization-n2.md.
